name: Jonathan
overview: Jonathan was a male Levite known as the son of Joiada, as recorded in Nehemiah 12:11. His identity is primarily established through his lineage within the tribe of Levi. There are no additional personal notes or distinguishing details beyond his familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Jonathan means 'gift of y-h-v-h,' reflecting a recognition of divine blessing. Another related name, Johanan, means 'y-h-v-h is gracious,' indicating a theme of God's favor in these names. Neither name is described as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Jonathan is identified as the son of Joiada according to Nehemiah 12:11, with Joiada himself being the son of Jaddua. These relationships provide a clear paternal lineage within the Levite tribe, emphasizing Jonathan's place in a priestly family.
scriptureSignificance: Jonathan's significance in Scripture is tied to his priestly heritage as a Levite and his position as the son of Joiada. Although detailed personal achievements are not recorded, his inclusion in the genealogical record highlights the continuity of the Levitical priesthood. This lineage underscores the faithfulness of God's covenant people through successive generations.

keyEvents.event: Nearly executed by Saul for breaking fast
